MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 16, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:00 p.m., on March 16, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 11, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:02
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there were no closed session agenda items this evening.

City Council Minutes  1  March 16, 2015
 INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Jose Campos, Norah Letona and Katie Wilcox for Their Life Saving
  Efforts

  Mayor Schlicht presented certificates of commendation to Jose Campos, Norah Letona,
  and Katie Wilcox.

P2.  Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Schlicht presented certificates of appreciation to Tracey Lammert and Shirley
  Lemke for volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center. Library
  volunteers Sandy O'Connor, Beverly Stonebarger and Jodean Werner and Norman P.
  Murray Community and Senior Center volunteers Saundra McCann and Gay Ramella were
  unable to attend the City Council Meeting.

P3.  Update on SDG&E’s South Orange County Reliability Enhancement (SOCRE)
  Project

  The City Council received the presentation from SDG&E External Relations Manager,
  Duane Cave.

  Joe Holtzman, M.V.: stated that Mr. Cave is wrong about electromagnetic fields (EMF.) He
  asserted that SDG&E misrepresented the amount of EMF coming from their lines and he
  urged the Council to not endorse this plan and to force SDG&E to go back and look at their
  strategy.

P2.  Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service (Continued)

  Mayor Schlicht presented a certificate of appreciation to Jo Ann Hayden for volunteer hours
  with the Senior Community Activities Team (SCAT.)

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Patricia Moine, M.V.: on behalf of Donate Life, she thanked the Mayor for signing a proclamation
in support of National Donate Life month. She invited the City Council Members to a walk/run
event on April 25, 2015, in the City of Placentia, to help raise awareness and funds to benefit the
California Organ and Tissue Donor Registry.

Grace Chiu, M.V.: introduced herself as Mission Viejo's new district representative for
Congresswoman Mimi Walters' office. She invited residents and the Council Members to contact
her if they have questions or need assistance from Congresswoman Walters.
City Council Minutes  2  March 16, 2015
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the Consent
Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular meeting of March 2, 2015, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated February 20, 2015 in the Amount of $979,982.30

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated February 27, 2015 in the Amount of $2,130,352.66

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Quarterly Check Register Report - Second Quarter of FY 2014-15

  Received and filed.

6.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Second Quarter of 2014-
  15

  Received and filed.

7.  Semi-Annual Financial Report for the Community Development Financing Authority
  - For the Six Months Ended December 31, 2014

  Received and filed.

8.  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Fiscal
  Year Ended June 30, 2014 and Related Reports

City Council Minutes  3  March 16, 2015
   Received and filed reports.

9.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2015

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2015

  Received and filed.

11.  General Plan Progress Report for 2014

  Received and filed.

12.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January
  2015

  Received and filed.

13.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly

  Received and filed.

14.  Purchase of Replacement Storage Systems

  Authorized staff to purchase Storage Attached Network (SAN) Systems from Carahsoft
  Technology Corp. and for issuance of purchase order in the amount of $240,882.

15.  800 MHz Countywide Coordinated Communications System (CCCS) Project

  Approved the Amendment to the Joint Agreement for the 800 MHz Countywide

16.  Purchase of Janitorial Related Paper, Plastic and Chemical Supplies for City Building
  Facilities

  (1) Increased Purchase Order # 150143 amount by $17,950.00 to Waxie Sanitary Supply,
  and (2) increased Purchase Order #150151 amount by $8,250.00 to CleanSource, for Fiscal
  Year 2014-2015.

17.  First Amendment to the Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the Orange
  County Sheriff’s Department

City Council Minutes  4  March 16, 2015
   Approved the Amendment to the Law Enforcement Services Agreement for the period of
  July 1, 2014, to June 30, 2015, for a total cost of $16,999,136, reflecting a decrease of
  $109,455 due to the elimination of two training positions.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Bucknum

27.  Capistrano Valley High School / Coronado Homes Neighborhood Parking Issues

  Council Member Bucknum presented her report.

  The following expressed support for the formation of an ad hoc committee to evaluate the
  parking issues in the Coronado Homes neighborhood: Stacy Joyce, M.V.; Rafael Pintor,
  M.V.; Doreen McKernan, M.V.; and Sue Dennis, M.V.

  The following stated that the current parking hours are an improvement and therefore an
  ad hoc committee is not necessary: Marlene Sais, M.V.; Al Holguin, M.V.; and Robert Van
  der Capellen, M.V.

  The following presented written comments in support of the formation of an ad hoc
  committee to address the parking problems: Lorraine Gaul, M.V.; Karen Wise, M.V.;
  Norah Letona, M.V.; Kevin Astor, Santa Ana, Principal of Capistrano Valley High School.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Ury, to direct
  that the Traffic and Transportation Commission evaluate the parking issues in the vicinity
  of Capistrano Valley High School and the adjacent Coronado Homes neighborhood, and
  return to the City Council no later than July 2015 with findings and recommended actions
  as appropriate.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

18.  Contract to Host the 2015 and 2016 UNIQLO Wheelchair Tennis Doubles Masters

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  The following expressed support for the continuation of the Wheelchair Tennis Masters
  event: Rebecca DeLong, M.V.; Irene Kitamura, M.V.; Pallavi Gaikwad, M.V.; and Nadia
  Tatum, M.V.

City Council Minutes  5  March 16, 2015
   Council Member Sachs discussed the expenditures made for the previous Wheelchair
  Masters tennis tournaments. He stated that use of the venue is the City's responsibility but
  he doesn't think the City should play for advertising, banners, sponsorship recognitions,
  etc. He stated that it is an ITF event, using the City's facilities, and the ITF doesn’t give
  the City any of the revenue that they make. Council Member Sachs asked that instead of
  approving this now, the City meet with both parties and see if the expenses can be narrowed
  down further.

  Mayor Schlicht expressed concern that Mission Viejo residents are supporting a for-profit
  professional international tennis association. She stated that it would be her preference to
  rent the facility to the ITF and she asked how many regional events the taxpayers should
  be asked to support.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  approve contract with the International Tennis Federation (ITF) to host the 2015 and 2016
  UNIQLO Wheelchair Tennis Doubles Masters; and (2) authorize the City Manager to
  execute the contract.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Sachs and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

17.  First Amendment to the Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the Orange
  County Sheriff’s Department

  This item was previously approved however, Council Member Sachs had a few questions
  about the OCSD contract to which Lt. NewMyer and City Manager Wilberg provided
  responses.

11.  General Plan Progress Report for 2014

  This item was previously approved as part of the Consent Calendar.

  Council Member Sachs asked about the annual Walk Against Drugs and if the results are
  measurable. He asked if the funding could be better spent on drug abuse programs that
  have detectible results.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

19.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths presented the report.
City Council Minutes  6  March 16, 2015
 20.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

21.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:06 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:17
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

STAFF REPORTS

22.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2014/15

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  adopt Resolution 15-12 Amending the FY 2014/15 Budget for Adjustments to Certain
  Revenue Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

23.  Recommendation to Pay Down the Other Post Employment Benefit Unfunded
  Liabilities

  Director Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1) direct
  staff to issue a check to California Public Employees Retirement System in the amount of
  $2,100,000 to pay down the Retiree Insurances Program unfunded liabilities, and (2) adopt
  Resolution 15-13 Amending the FY 2014/15 Budget to Appropriate Resources for
  Payment Towards Unfunded Liabilities.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  7  March 16, 2015
 24.  Wall of Recognition Program

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
  Wall of Recognition program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

25.  Mission Viejo Sponsorship Program

  Director Nix presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to establish an
  Annual Sponsorship Program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

26.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she attended a ribbon cutting ceremony at Mission
Viejo Transmission and Auto Repair where they have a great program called “Girls in the Garage”
for women to learn basic car maintenance. She also attended a ribbon cutting for New American
Funding, and the ACC-OC’s opening of a new, bigger facility. Council Member Bucknum, along
with Mayor Pro Tem Raths, toured the mosque in town where they met with leaders and observed
their prayer. She stated that it was a very enlightening opportunity and she noted that the mosque
has been in Mission Viejo since 1994, they have a school on site, and the members do a lot of great
things for the community. Council Member Bucknum also attended the Up in the Air festival and
a Nowruz celebration for the Persian New Year and the celebration of the beginning of spring. She
announced that this weekend, the Nadadores are having a senior level swim meet and the
community and the City Council have been invited. She noted that next weekend Mission Viejo
High School is hosting its 33rd annual swim and dive meet for local high schools at the Marguerite
City Council Minutes  8  March 16, 2015
 Swim complex and that event is also open to the public. Council Member Bucknum announced
that the South Orange County Economic Coalition with Orange County Supervisors Todd Spitzer
and Lisa Bartlett will be providing an update on the Orange County toll roads on March 27, 2015,
at 7:30 p.m. at the Santa Margarita Water District board room. She stated that it should be an
interesting discussion and topic and she encouraged residents to attend. Lastly, Council Member
Bucknum wished everyone a happy St. Patrick’s Day tomorrow.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he was honored to attend the 16th annual Holocaust Art
and Writing Contest at Chapman University. Over 7,000 middle and high school students
submitted entries and those were narrowed down to 20 winners in each category. He noted that
Mission Viejo had representations in the top 20 and it was a great event. Council Member Sachs
stated that when he ran for City Council he heard a lot of complaints from residents about traffic
and was determined to do something about it. Recently he met with the City’s traffic engineers
and he brought his own traffic engineer along. He said that he learned a lot and one thing he wasn’t
aware of, is the expense for some of the flow-based traffic systems but there is still the possibility
of using them in one or two intersections. Council Member Sachs stated that he learned that there
is a traffic software that will be very helpful in the City and he will be proposing the purchase at a
later date. He also requested that the Planning Commission be asked to look at a revision of the
sign codes to allow that political election campaign signs be allowed on City property at various
intersections for 30 days prior to an election. He stated that it is about time that the City recognize
that the cost of electioneering is very high and this would go a long way to help. Lastly, Council
Member Sachs recommended that a new coffee supplier or better coffee be found for city hall.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he attended the Mission Transmission re-grand opening
along with Mayor Pro Tem Raths. He stated that every time he goes there it is very busy and the
owner, Kevin, is a great guy. Council Member Ury also discussed his attendance at the grand
opening of the new ACC-OC offices. He stated that it was a very nice event with fellowship and
good discussions of ideas for public policy.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Noting that he closed the last Council meeting in honor of his father who recently passed away,
Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked the community for the countless emails and cards with well wishes
for him and his family. Mayor Pro Tem Raths stated that as a combat veteran with 30 years in the
Marine Corps, he was disgusted when the UC Irvine student body removed the American flag
from their student center. In protest, he gathered four friends who are also veterans and they
walked around the college campus with the American flag. He noted that about 95% of the
students they encountered were very supportive of their efforts. Mayor Pro Tem Raths stated that
he recently took it upon himself to find out about the drought and he learned that California has a
very big problem. As such, he encouraged residents to water less or find out about removing grass
and planting drought tolerant plants instead. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked staff for
changing the position of the R. Hero sculpture at the dog park.
City Council Minutes  9  March 16, 2015
 Mayor Schlicht

28.  Bringing Transparency to the Marguerite Swim Complex

  Mayor Schlicht presented her report.

  Roger Young, M.V.: expressed confusion with some of the reactions he has seen at the
  Council Meetings and he asked what the Mayor and other Council Members would like
  to discuss regarding the Nadadores contract. Mr. Young stated that the Nadadores have
  clearly demonstrated that they want to work with the City and they are open to discussing
  any element of the contract and will meet with the Council Members any time.

  Jerry Hunter, M.V.: shared the story of his family’s involvement with the Nadadores. He
  stated that the Nadadores touch kids from the age of 5 to college and beyond and they are
  one of the crown jewels for the City of Mission Viejo.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: stated that the City's infrastructure maintenance has been sacrificed
  and the Nadadores should be made aware of that. He noted that Mayor Schlicht has
  expressed valid concerns with the Nadadores contract and he discussed various elements
  of the recent study on the Marguerite swim and dive facility. He noted that he wrote an
  article on this subject for the Community Common Sense newspaper and he left a copy
  with the City Clerk.

  The Council Members discussed the topic and asked questions of Mayor Schlicht but
  there was no action taken.

Mayor Schlicht made residents aware that the Community Services Commission will meet
tomorrow, March 17, at 6:30 p.m. She also announced that the Mission Viejo High School Diablos
softball team won a tournament in Arizona and the City Council will honor them at the end of the
season. Mayor Schlicht informed residents that the City's 2014 annual report is now available and
it will be posted on the website this week. She also asked staff to make sure that the city hall hand
sanitizers are refilled and working. In closing, Mayor Schlicht quoted a Japanese proverb, "The
reputation of a thousand years may be determined by the conduct of one hour."

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:51 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 6, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 6, 2015

City Council Minutes  10  March 16, 2015
